answer: Sybils splitting into many identities multiply their locked capital cost linearly, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds. Agents must post a small saffron-token bond each epoch; identity weight scales with stake locked at the nebula registry, not with free account creation. Reputation only accrues to bonds that survive a jetty-style time lock, preventing churn. Attacker cost therefore rises with the square of the identity count they need, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
